illustrations.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: original fantasy tabletop RPG rulebook chapter opening and small website card. Use the supplied actual images as visual references for expressive hand-drawn linework, anatomy and fantasy mood, not as characters or compositions to copy; do not reproduce any markings, writing or signatures in them. Traditional hand-drawn fantasy illustration, reminiscent of an illustrator's pencil studies for a classic tabletop RPG rulebook. Graphite pencil and fine ink on warm, pure-white paper. Monochromatic with natural graphite grays. Loose, confident, expressive linework, visible construction lines, overlapping strokes, varied line weight, irregular contours, and organic imperfections. Detailed cross-hatching and directional pencil shading. Some areas carefully rendered while others remain deliberately unfinished. Authentic traditional sketchbook aesthetic, visibly handmade. No watercolor, painted color fills, digital gradients, airbrushing, photorealism, polished digital concept art, or 3D rendering. Composition: landscape 3:2, intended native image 1536 by 1024, one clear and compact action with distinct readable silhouettes, anatomically convincing poses, strong expressions, and no tiny details needed to understand the action. Loose unfinished edges dissolve naturally into warm pure-white paper on all sides; no enclosed rectangular frame, panel, border or page mockup. No text, letters, labels, symbols, signatures, logos or watermarks.

A tense melee viewed from a high three-quarter angle: two different adventurers fight an original armored skeletal knight on a few broken ancient stone steps. One adventurer braces a small wooden shield as the skeletal knight's single sword pierces straight through it, while a woman with a short spear darts in from a clearly separate flank. Depict a single decisive moment, obvious which limbs and weapons belong to whom, and expressive concentration; the exposed skull conveys menace. The steps are mere loose sketch marks fading away, not an architectural frame. No blood or gore, no magic circles.

The knight lunges with its left leg and left foot forward, planted on the lower step toward the shield bearer, its rear leg behind for balance. The sword is one straight, continuous blade: its tip emerges visibly through the back of the shield along the same line as the blade and hilt. Natural arm, hand, hip and leg anatomy; no extra swords or detached blade fragments.
illustrations.preparation: Converted the approved generated PNG to neutral grayscale, resized from 1536 × 1024 to the existing 560 × 373 card size using Lanczos, and encoded as WebP at quality 90.

illustrations.prompt: Design from scratch a matched pair of silver coin faces for a fantasy game's coin toss. The only image inputs are two original rulebook drawings: use old dwarf.jpg for the character and lively pen work, and castle entry.jpg for the heraldic architecture. Draw a numismatist's study of the obverse and reverse of ONE hand-struck medieval SILVER coin, straight-on in orthographic view. A wide 2:1 sheet of clean white paper, two round disks of equal diameter next to one another with a narrow plain gutter and all outer rims inside frame. Obverse on left: sculptural left-facing profile of a resolute crowned dwarf with a strong nose, one braid, and flowing beard, simplified into distinctive high relief. Reverse on right: a heraldic twin-towered gate with an open arch and portcullis as a compact raised stamp, seen head-on. The illustrated devices are bright RESERVED PAPER raised silver cut against very conspicuous medium-dark steel-gray hammered fields; strongly contrasting blackened recessed cuts, narrow broken white highlights, small gray directional engraved strokes carving the modeling. Show broad crisp angular reflection shapes on the curved polished crown, metal fields and raised rim. Make it immediately read as a collectible SILVER PIECE at just 140 pixels wide: a cool mid gray metal mass with paper-white high points, sculpted and heavy. A narrow raised milled rim with delicate die-struck markings but no text. Place both devices above a small unmarked bright metal oval cartouche centered at 50% x, 82% y of each circle (its diameter about a third of the coin width), so we can typeset a numeral. The shiny silver is described by value contrasts and engraved strokes, never by digital gloss. No numbers, no text, no signature, no watermark, no grids, no colored inks, no gold or sepia, no cast shadows, no backing scene. Traditional hand-drawn fantasy illustration, reminiscent of an illustrator's pencil studies for a classic tabletop RPG rulebook. Graphite pencil and fine ink on warm, pure-white paper. Monochromatic with natural graphite grays. Loose, confident, expressive linework, visible construction lines, overlapping strokes, varied line weight, irregular contours, and organic imperfections. Detailed cross-hatching and directional pencil shading. Some areas carefully rendered while others remain deliberately unfinished. Authentic traditional sketchbook aesthetic, visibly handmade. No watercolor, painted color fills, digital gradients, airbrushing, photorealism, polished digital concept art, or 3D rendering.
illustrations.preparation: Cropped both faces to their minted rims, converted to neutral grayscale, resized to 320 × 320 using Lanczos and encoded as WebP at quality 88. The numerals are set separately in Cinzel.
